scope: Tiny paired local contracts;root-owned runtime qualification is separate.

cases.title: Validate identities before defining a winner
cases.input_contract: Reject an input unless event_id is known, positive and unique and entity is known. Allow missing event_time under the declared last-priority policy. Return Unit/None on success.
cases.expected: The eight-event fixture passes;adding another copy of event 1 fails. Missing-time event 7 is allowed.
cases.verification: Assert normal acceptance and explicit rejection after unioning a duplicate identity.

cases.title: Rank all candidates with an explicit NULL rule
cases.input_contract: Add candidate_rank using row_number per entity, descending event_time with NULL last, then descending event_id. Keep all eight rows.
cases.verification: Assert the full ID/rank table and input count 8.

cases.title: Select stable winners across physical layouts
cases.input_contract: Validate candidates, rank them and retain rank 1. Compare winner IDs after repartitioning to 1,3 and 4 partitions, then compare an equivalentSQL row_number query.
cases.expected: Every case yields event IDs[3,6,8], one per entity. SQL returns the same literal winners.
cases.verification: Assert exact winners in every layout and SQL, not just equal row counts.

cases.title: Prove why timestamp-only ordering is incomplete
cases.input_contract: Use dense_rank ordered only by descending event_time with NULL last, returning all rank 1 candidates. Report the candidate IDs rather than choosing an arbitrary winner.
cases.expected: Top-time candidates[2,3,5,6,8]. EntitiesA andB each have two admissible candidates under the incomplete rule.
cases.verification: Assert the five candidate identities and the two ambiguous entity keys. Do not require unstable executions to change output.

cases.title: Distinguish occurrence totals from time-peer totals
cases.input_contract: Return event_id, rows_total, peer_total. ROWS uses ascending time NULL last then ID and an unbounded-preceding/current-row frame. RANGE uses only ascending time NULL last over the same cumulative boundary.
cases.verification: Assert all eight tuples, especially tied IDs 2/3 and the missing-time event 7.

cases.title: Interpret lag without claiming strict temporal availability
cases.input_contract: Using ascending time NULL last then event_id, return event_id, previous_id, gap_seconds. Lag the event identity and time, then subtract epoch seconds.
cases.verification: Assert the complete identity/gap rows and explain zero gaps and the known previous ID with unknown duration.
